name: M15 realized-semivariance imbalance transition follow and fade screening batch

source_references.citation: Liu, Lu, Li and Wang (2023), Time series momentum and reversal: intraday information from realized semivariance, Journal of Empirical Finance 72, 54-77
source_references.supports: Opened accepted manuscript studies 31 Chinese commodity futures in 2007-2018 using 5-minute returns aggregated over prior weeks to tune daily 20-day momentum. It supports semivariance as an information decomposition, not this 60-minute M1 FX imbalance threshold or 30-60-minute response.

research.evidence_summary: A primary study supports signed realized semivariance as information about daily commodity-momentum reversals, with major market and horizon mismatch. The fixed intrahour imbalance transition and both response signs are therefore a compact speculative falsification, not a claimed edge.

feasibility.rationale: Uses only causal M1 closes, completed M15 timing, prior ATR, supported fills/stops and same-day exits. V2 compatibility remains unconfirmed.

market.base_timeframe: M1 with London-aligned M15 decision times
market.session: Weekday signals at completed London M15 bars ending 09:00 through 13:45; every exit due no later than 15:00

data.frequency: Interval-start M1 OHLC; decision times are Europe/London wall-clock M15 boundaries
data.minimum_history: Sufficient valid observed M15 true ranges for ATR96 through t-1 and 76 consecutive valid M1 closes ending at signal time
preprocessing: Treat M1 timestamp ts as [ts,ts+1 minute); require 76 consecutive unique valid candles/closes for the union of prior and current 60-return windows
Valid OHLC is finite and positive with high>=max(open,close), low<=min(open,close), high>=low; duplicates or any missing candle invalidate the event
Use chart/bid one-minute log close returns; current window contains the latest 60 returns through signal close and prior window is the 60-return window ending exactly 15 returns earlier
For each window sum squared positive returns into RS_plus and squared negative returns into RS_minus; zero returns enter neither sum
Compute observed-sequence M15 TR and Wilder ATR96 through t-1; routine earlier elapsed gaps remain represented, but the 76-close event union must be physically contiguous
Use IANA Europe/London rules and canonical UTC storage
dependencies: V2 causal M1 and M15 boundary handling
V2 resolved signal-time spread, commission and slippage
limitations: Primary evidence uses weekly semivariance and daily Chinese commodity momentum, not intrahour FX direction
The 0.50 threshold and 60-minute window are unvalidated
Squared returns can be dominated by one M1 jump and remain microstructure-sensitive
Six correlated symbols/four cells are not independent

hypothesis.behavior: A first transition to strong positive or negative realized-semivariance dominance within the latest hour may continue with the dominant signed variation or fade over 30-60 minutes.
hypothesis.mechanism: Signed variation imbalance may distinguish one-sided information flow from balanced volatility, while the opposite sign tests short-horizon overreaction.
works_when: The imbalance transition captures a meaningful change rather than one bad tick
One response sign survives both holds and costs
fails_when: The source horizon does not transfer
Squared-return dominance merely relabels a shock
falsifiable_predictions: Both hold cells for one response mode are positive under normal and doubled costs
The 60-minute center is positive in both UTC halves and at least three symbols
Both cells survive common five-date removal

definitions.name: one_minute_returns
definitions.formula: r_j=ln(close_j)-ln(close_{j-1}) over consecutive chart/bid M1 closes
definitions.timing: Current window is the latest 60 returns through completed signal close; prior window ends 15 returns earlier

definitions.name: realized_semivariances
definitions.formula: RS_plus=sum(r_j^2 * 1[r_j>0]); RS_minus=sum(r_j^2 * 1[r_j<0]) over the specified 60-return window
definitions.timing: Computed separately for prior and current fully observed windows

definitions.name: semivariance_imbalance
definitions.timing: Q_prior ends at t-1 M15 boundary; Q_current ends at t boundary

definitions.name: imbalance_entry_direction
definitions.formula: +1 iff abs(Q_prior)<0.50 AND Q_current>=0.50; -1 iff abs(Q_prior)<0.50 AND Q_current<=-0.50; otherwise 0
definitions.timing: Known at completed t close; direct extreme-to-opposite-extreme flips do not trigger

definitions.name: atr96_prior
definitions.formula: Wilder ATR96 over valid observed London M15 true ranges through t-1
definitions.timing: Frozen before signal t; require finite positive

definitions.name: trade_side
definitions.formula: imbalance_entry_direction for FOLLOW_IMBALANCE and -imbalance_entry_direction for FADE_IMBALANCE

entries.long_condition: eligible imbalance transition AND ((direction=+1 AND FOLLOW_IMBALANCE) OR (direction=-1 AND FADE_IMBALANCE)) AND cell flat
entries.short_condition: eligible imbalance transition AND ((direction=-1 AND FOLLOW_IMBALANCE) OR (direction=+1 AND FADE_IMBALANCE)) AND cell flat
entries.signal_time: Completed London M15 boundary ending 09:00 through 13:45 on weekday when signal time plus holding_minutes<=15:00
entries.execution_details: Enter at final M1 chart/bid close of completed boundary; V2 applies resolved/fallback spread, commission and slippage. Entry candle cannot trigger the stop; management starts next M1.
entries.order_type: Market order at supported signal-close execution
restrictions: One open position per symbol per cell
All 76 M1 closes in the union window must be physically consecutive and valid
Persistent same-side imbalance at or beyond threshold cannot retrigger; direct extreme sign flips do not trigger until Q first returns strictly inside abs(Q)<0.50

exits.stop_loss: Long bid-chart stop=signal_close_bid-atr96_prior; short=signal_close_bid+atr96_prior. Long triggers bid, short executable ask; adverse gaps fill at worse executable open with costs.
exits.time_exit: Exit at M1 close ending exactly signal_time plus holding_minutes; invalid M1 in (entry_time,due_exit_time] fails affected cells; valid due bar resolves STOP_LOSS before TIME_EXIT
exits.maximum_holding: At most 60 minutes and never after 15:00 Europe/London
exits.end_of_session: No entry matures after 15:00; post-entry defects fail only affected cells

risk.position_sizing: Each cell owns isolated portfolio; same-timestamp symbols within a cell size from common pre-entry equity so chart stop risk is 0.25% before costs; no state crosses cells.
risk.gross_exposure_limit: Per cell at most six symbols and 1.50% aggregate initial stop risk; no cap shared across four portfolios
risk.leverage: Use lower of stop-risk size and V2 limits; skip unrepresentable size
risk.concurrent_positions: Within each cell one per symbol and six total; four cells independently track all state

experiment.baseline: 60-return signed semivariance imbalance/0.50 rising edge/one-ATR stop; FOLLOW_IMBALANCE; hold=60
robustness_tests: Report all four cells and retain full breadth ledger
Report symbols and UTC-midpoint halves; midpoint close belongs first half
Double spread, commission and slippage individually
For each mode center hold=60 remove five best normal-cost London dates from both hold cells; require both normal/doubled net R positive
For both cells use eligible London weekdays including zeros and 10000 circular five-date bootstrap resamples seed 2026022; center lower bound must exceed zero
Mode advances only if hold=60 center and hold=30 neighbor both pass
Report positive/negative transitions, zero-denominator windows, invalid union windows and maximum single-return share of realized variance
costs: Use resolved/fallback spread, commission and slippage at each fill
benchmarks: Opposite response mode on identical transitions
experiment.multiple_testing: Count all 348 selectable R007-R022 cells, two R008 diagnostics, the Liu et al. semivariance-tuned momentum family, and every named shock, path, skewness, semivariance and higher-moment trial. Cross-batch promotion uses full ledger; incomplete IDs prohibit confirmation; no best-cell/family rescue.
rejection_criteria: Reject mode unless both holds positive normal/doubled
Reject if center non-positive either UTC half or fewer than three symbols positive each half
Reject if center fewer than 300 trades
Reject if five-date removal makes either cell non-positive
Reject if center bootstrap lower bound not above zero
Reject promotion on required-cell data failure
Never access holdout without explicit authorization for separately frozen version

pseudocode: Maintain a valid consecutive M1 close buffer and prior-only observed-sequence M15 ATR96.
At each eligible completed M15 boundary compute prior and current 60-return positive/negative semivariances from the 76-close union.
Compute Q only for positive total realized variance and trigger only strict-inside to inclusive-extreme transitions.
Map follow/fade and enter flat cells at signal close.
From next M1 process stop before due exit; fail only affected cells.
Publish four cells and full robustness/ledger rows.
required_libraries: existing V2 candle, timezone, cost, fill and R-accounting components
edge_cases: all-zero returns make Q undefined and suppress event
direct extreme sign flip is suppressed
one missing or duplicate M1 candle suppresses event
adverse gap uses worse executable open
implementation.computational_requirements: One causal M1 pass per symbol with rolling signed-square sums, M15 ATR state and four isolated portfolios.
known_backtester_gaps: Queue waits for V2 rolling M1 semivariance, boundary/fill and result-ledger compatibility confirmation
